subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 35-year-old man is evaluated for a pituitary prolactinoma, a pancreatic gastrinoma causing recurrent peptic ulcers (Zollinger-Ellison syndrome), and hypercalcemia due to a parathyroid adenoma. His father and paternal uncle had similar tumors. All MEN syndromes show autosomal dominant inheritance.
question: Which of the following best characterizes his syndrome?

options.text: MEN2A with parathyroid hyperplasia, medullary thyroid carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma
MEN2B with mucosal neuromas and a marfanoid habitus
MEN1 with pituitary, pancreatic endocrine, and parathyroid tumors
Von Hippel-Lindau disease with hemangioblastomas and renal cell carcinoma
Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia with parathyroid hyperplasia

explanation_correct: MEN1 is characterized by the 3 P's: Pituitary tumors (prolactin or GH), Pancreatic endocrine tumors (Zollinger-Ellison syndrome/gastrinoma, insulinoma, VIPoma, glucagonoma), and Parathyroid adenomas. It is caused by mutation of the MEN1 tumor suppressor gene encoding menin on chromosome 11 and is associated with angiofibromas, collagenomas, and meningiomas. Like all MEN syndromes, it has autosomal dominant inheritance. This patient's pituitary, pancreatic, and parathyroid tumors are the classic triad.

explanation_incorrect.A: MEN2A consists of parathyroid hyperplasia, medullary thyroid carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma — not pituitary or pancreatic endocrine tumors.
explanation_incorrect.B: MEN2B features medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, and marfanoid habitus, not the 3 P's.
explanation_incorrect.D: Von Hippel-Lindau disease causes hemangioblastomas, renal cell carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma, not the pituitary-pancreas-parathyroid triad.
explanation_incorrect.E: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is a calcium-sensing receptor disorder with hypocalciuria, not a multiple tumor syndrome.

educationalObjective: MEN1 is the autosomal dominant 3 P's syndrome: pituitary, pancreatic endocrine, and parathyroid tumors from menin loss on chromosome 11.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 40-year-old woman is diagnosed with medullary thyroid carcinoma and a unilateral pheochromocytoma. Genetic testing reveals a germline RET mutation. Her physician explains that she has a RET-driven MEN syndrome and compares it with the other RET-driven subtype.
question: Which of the following findings is part of MEN2A but NOT part of MEN2B?

options.text: Parathyroid hyperplasia
Medullary thyroid carcinoma
Pheochromocytoma
Mucosal neuromas
Marfanoid habitus

explanation_correct: MEN2A consists of parathyroid hyperplasia, medullary thyroid carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma — the 2 P's and 1 M. MEN2B consists of medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas (oral/intestinal ganglioneuromatosis), and marfanoid habitus — the 1 P and 2 M's. Parathyroid disease is unique to MEN2A among the RET-driven syndromes. Both subtypes are autosomal dominant and caused by mutations in the RET protooncogene on chromosome 10.

explanation_incorrect.B: Medullary thyroid carcinoma occurs in both MEN2A and MEN2B, so it does not distinguish them.
explanation_incorrect.C: Pheochromocytoma occurs in both MEN2A and MEN2B, so it is not unique to MEN2A.
explanation_incorrect.D: Mucosal neuromas are a feature of MEN2B, not MEN2A.
explanation_incorrect.E: Marfanoid habitus is characteristic of MEN2B, not MEN2A.

educationalObjective: Parathyroid hyperplasia distinguishes MEN2A (2 P's, 1 M) from MEN2B (1 P, 2 M's), which instead has mucosal neuromas and marfanoid habitus.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 22-year-old man has a tall, slender habitus with long extremities and multiple painless bumps on the tongue and lips. He has episodic hypertension and an elevated serum calcitonin. Endoscopy shows oral and intestinal ganglioneuromatosis. A maternal uncle died of early thyroid cancer.
question: Which of the following best identifies his syndrome and its distinguishing features?

options.text: MEN1 — pituitary, pancreatic endocrine, and parathyroid tumors
MEN2A — parathyroid hyperplasia, medullary thyroid carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma
Neurofibromatosis type 1 — cafe-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, and pheochromocytoma
MEN2B — medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, and marfanoid habitus
Carney complex — spotty skin pigmentation, myxomas, and endocrine tumors

explanation_correct: MEN2B is an autosomal dominant RET-associated syndrome consisting of medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas (oral/intestinal ganglioneuromatosis), and a marfanoid habitus. The 1 P and 2 M's mnemonic captures the single pheochromocytoma and the two M's. This patient's elevated calcitonin indicates medullary thyroid carcinoma from parafollicular C cells, while the mucosal neuromas and marfanoid body habitus are the distinguishing clues for MEN2B rather than MEN2A.

explanation_incorrect.A: MEN1 is the 3 P's (pituitary, pancreatic endocrine, parathyroid) and does not include medullary thyroid carcinoma, mucosal neuromas, or marfanoid habitus.
explanation_incorrect.B: MEN2A includes parathyroid hyperplasia but lacks the mucosal neuromas and marfanoid habitus that define MEN2B.
explanation_incorrect.C: Neurofibromatosis type 1 features cafe-au-lait macules and neurofibromas with pheochromocytoma, but not this neuromatous/calcitonin triad.
explanation_incorrect.E: Carney complex is a distinct autosomal dominant syndrome with lentigines and myxomas, not a RET-driven MEN subtype.

educationalObjective: Mucosal neuromas plus marfanoid habitus with medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma identify MEN2B.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A genetic counselor reviews two branches of a family with multiple endocrine tumors. One branch has pituitary and parathyroid tumors; the other has medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma. Both patterns show vertical transmission consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance. She reviews the causative genes and their chromosomal locations.
question: Which of the following correctly pairs each syndrome with its causative gene and chromosomal location?

options.text: MEN1 — RET protooncogene, chromosome 10; MEN2A — menin tumor suppressor, chromosome 11
MEN1 — RET protooncogene, chromosome 11; MEN2A — menin tumor suppressor, chromosome 10
MEN1 — menin tumor suppressor, chromosome 10; MEN2A — RET protooncogene, chromosome 11
MEN1 — MEN1 tumor suppressor (menin), chromosome 11; MEN2A — RET tumor suppressor, chromosome 10
MEN1 — MEN1 tumor suppressor (menin), chromosome 11; MEN2A/2B — RET protooncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase), chromosome 10

explanation_correct: MEN1 results from mutation of the MEN1 tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 11, which encodes menin. MEN2A and MEN2B result from germline mutations in RET on chromosome 10, a protooncogene encoding a receptor tyrosine kinase. All MEN syndromes are autosomal dominant. Option E is the only choice that assigns the correct gene, chromosome, and gene class to each syndrome.

explanation_incorrect.A: The genes and chromosomes are swapped: menin/MEN1 is on chromosome 11, while RET is on chromosome 10.
explanation_incorrect.B: RET is located on chromosome 10 and menin on chromosome 11, and they belong to different MEN subtypes.
explanation_incorrect.C: The chromosomes are reversed — MEN1/menin is on chromosome 11 and RET is on chromosome 10.
explanation_incorrect.D: The chromosomes are correct, but RET is a protooncogene encoding a receptor tyrosine kinase, not a tumor suppressor gene.

educationalObjective: MEN1 is a chromosome 11 tumor suppressor (menin) syndrome; MEN2A/2B are chromosome 10 RET protooncogene syndromes.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 6-year-old girl from a family with MEN2A undergoes genetic testing and is found to carry a disease-causing RET mutation. She is asymptomatic, serum calcitonin is normal, and neck ultrasound shows no mass. Her parents ask about the plan to prevent thyroid cancer.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate management for this child?

options.text: Observation with annual serum calcitonin measurements only
Prophylactic thyroidectomy
External beam radiation to the neck
Total parathyroidectomy
Initiation of somatostatin analogs

explanation_correct: In MEN2A, medullary thyroid carcinoma is a neoplasm of parafollicular C cells that secretes calcitonin and is aggressively invasive at an early age. Because carriers of a disease-causing RET mutation are at near-certain risk, prophylactic thyroidectomy is required, often in early childhood and guided by the specific RET mutation. Waiting for calcitonin elevation or a sonographic mass would risk missing the curative window. This is a distinctive management point tested for RET-associated MEN2 syndromes.

explanation_incorrect.A: Surveillance alone is inadequate — prophylactic thyroidectomy is recommended because medullary thyroid carcinoma is invasive and early.
explanation_incorrect.C: External beam radiation is not the standard prophylaxis; surgery removes the at-risk parafollicular C cells directly.
explanation_incorrect.D: Parathyroid hyperplasia in MEN2A is managed separately and does not warrant prophylactic total parathyroidectomy in an asymptomatic child.
explanation_incorrect.E: Somatostatin analogs help control neuroendocrine tumor secretion, not prevent RET-driven medullary thyroid carcinoma.

educationalObjective: RET mutation carriers in MEN2 require prophylactic thyroidectomy because medullary thyroid carcinoma is early and invasive.
